interpretation_boundaries: 129 and 83 are sums of positive/negative per-utterance edit-distance differences, not counts of every individual newly introduced/fixed character error; within-utterance fixes and regressions can cancel.
Exact-correct means equality to the normalized official reference, not a guarantee of acoustic correctness.
Specific character substitutions depend on one valid optimal alignment; ties can change error allocation while CER remains invariant.

Text examples alone cannot establish acoustic truth, correct homophone spelling/names, reference annotation quality, or a causal training mechanism. No audio listening or acoustic verification was performed.

Bootstrap intervals describe held-out utterance/speaker resampling sensitivity of this paired checkpoint comparison, not training-seed variance or uncertainty of the fixed official-test arithmetic. Speaker cluster inference has only 20 observed clusters.
